title: Why Donating Old Clothes Is Better Than Throwing Them Away
excerpt: Every year millions of clothes end up in landfills. Here's why donating is the smarter, greener choice.
fullContent:
Every year, over 92 million tonnes of textile waste ends up in landfills globally. That old t-shirt you haven't worn in two years? It could take up to 200 years to decompose in a landfill — releasing harmful methane gas along the way.

Donating clothes is one of the simplest and most impactful things you can do for the planet. When you donate through platforms like Sharly, your clothes get a second life — worn by someone who needs them, reducing the demand for new fast fashion production.

Fast fashion is one of the top polluting industries in the world. Every new garment produced uses massive amounts of water, energy, and synthetic dyes that pollute rivers and ecosystems. By donating instead of discarding, you directly reduce this demand.

Beyond the environment, donating clothes helps real people. Families in need, students, workers starting new jobs — all benefit from access to clean, quality secondhand clothing. And with Sharly, you earn reward points for every donation.

So next time you're clearing your wardrobe, remember: donate instead of discard.
